3.	At 4:30 am on April 12 of the year N, militia troops from X started firing on Y, a fortress built on an island controlling the entrance to Charleston harbor. X had recently declared independence, and the bombardment was aimed at expelling what X’s militia considered an occupation force. The bombardment lasted for 34 hours before the occupants of Y surrendered. Remarkably, no one on either side was killed by the shelling itself, but two soldiers of the surrendering force died in an accidental explosion during the surrender ceremony. Years earlier as a student at military academy, P.G.T. Beauregard, the commander of the attacking militia, had learned artillery tactics from Robert Anderson, the commander holding Y. This incident marks the beginning of Z, the deadliest conflict in the history of the country. ID X (5 points), Y (10 points), Z (2 points), and N (3 points).
